title: From AA to USB-C: Follow Shrouk’s PCB Build with a Free 60-Day Trial
gist: Promotional getting-started guide for a free 60-day Siemens Xpedition Standard PCB design trial tied to engineer Shrouk El-Attar's 24-part tutorial series building a USB-C rechargeable module that fits a two-AA battery compartment. Little investable signal beyond Siemens' tutorial-led, creator-driven acquisition push for its PCB tools.

insights.claim: Siemens is offering a free 60-day trial of its Xpedition Standard PCB design software, paired with a 24-tutorial series (three per week for eight weeks) by engineering consultant Shrouk El-Attar promoted via LinkedIn.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows Siemens using free trials and creator-led tutorials to compete for PCB design users; minor go-to-market signal.
insights.locator: You can build along with her in Xpedition Standard.

insights.claim: The Xpedition Standard trial is installed via Siemens Software Center, takes around 20 minutes to install, and includes the Xpedition Designer and Xpedition Layout tools, with optional add-ons not required.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Low-friction onboarding is part of Siemens' effort to broaden its PCB tool funnel.

insights.claim: The Xpedition tutorial project designs a compact USB-C-rechargeable PCB module that fits a standard two-AA battery compartment, using the physical space and cable-access constraint to teach how schematic and layout decisions connect.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Illustrative teaching project only; no market claim made.
